    What cortex looks like when a post-stroke attempt fails

    VLS stroke, PS92–PS95, lesion left (brain maps: image left = ipsilesional). Final inputs: rebuilt attempts table, complete cam1, 3-D tongue; encoder analyses August-only pre. Every claim needs ≥ 3/4 animals. neural = imaging; lick = behaviour only. Details: docs/ENCODING_FINDINGS.md.

    Target vs executed · FINDINGS 2.4b

    1. Does cortex follow where the spout is, or where the tongue went? neural

    Encoding model with 6 spout categories (target) and soft-binned 3-D landing (executed, "softmax" bins: each lick weighted over the six spouts by its distance to each spout's pre-stroke landing centre). Values = what one set explains beyond the other.

    Chronic: target > executed 4/4 in both windows (width 1). Acute lick window: target ahead 3/4. Subacute mixed, pre no lead. The chronic lead holds across softmax widths (3/4 at the widest); the acute lead depends on width.
    Behaviour · the dissociation the contest uses

    2. Where the licks actually land lick

    Acute far-contra licks land like far-mid / far-ipsi licks (own bin −0.69, far mid +0.35, far ipsi +0.35; significant, 4/4). It shrinks but stays significant: subacute −0.38 / far mid +0.36, chronic −0.19 / far mid +0.20 (4/4) – part of the far-contra licks still land like far-mid licks chronically.
    Failed attempts · FINDINGS 2.8

    3. Is the far-contra code there when the attempt fails? neural

    Failed attempts lose the far-contra code (to the no-task floor in PS92/PS93) but are decoded as a far spout – distance kept, side lost (lick window 4/4). Nothing before the cue. Failed attempts stay low in every epoch; successful hits recover but stay below pre even chronically.
    Trial-type maps · FINDINGS 2.9

    4. What failed attempts look like on the cortex neural

    Same bilateral pattern as hits, smaller in 3/4 – but vs touch-matched pre-stroke misses only 2/4 (much of the drop = no touch / reward). Regionally: acute failed attempts reduce ipsilesional ALM / tjM1 more than contralesional (4/4); chronic hits increase tjM1 / SSp-m, more contralesionally, at every spout (4/4).
    Frozen pre-stroke encoder · FINDINGS 3.4

    5. Which part of the pre-stroke model carries the change neural

    Acute: the far-contra drop is predicted from how the animal now licks (lick part; target ≈ 0). Chronic: the response is larger than pre and the pre-stroke model does not predict it – the increase is in the residual.
    Is the chronic residual real? · FINDINGS 3.4

    6. The chronic residual: map statistics, per animal, and trend neural

    Pooled (each animal normalised by its own pre scale, nested bootstrap animals → sessions): weak – 80 / 41 / 48 of 2,022 bins (acute / subacute / chronic, lick), cluster test nothing. Within animal (sessions as unit; calibrated: random pre splits flag 0 bins in 20/20 per animal): chronic differs in 4/4 (lick: 522 / 110 / 135 / 113 bins), always on the contralesional side (PS92 bilateral anterolateral, PS93 / PS94 right anterolateral, PS95 right posterolateral); acute never. Trend: the pre-stroke rise did not continue (chronic far below the extrapolated 8-day trend) and the chronic level is flat over ~30 days – a raised plateau in 3/4 (not PS95), not ongoing drift.
    All-session encoder · FINDINGS 2 (Layer 2)

    7. Does the brain→behaviour mapping itself change? neural

    Chronic kernel change exceeds the pre-stroke baseline in 4/4, not a session-count effect, but it grows with time (PS93 / PS95); no single kernel group (lick, contact, target …) changes more than the baseline. Random-split null (August pre, no early/late) running.
